clue.text: You pays your money and takes your choice here

definitions.text: You pays your money and takes your choice here

blocks.clueFragment: You pays your money and takes your choice
blocks.note: surface reading: the old fairground catchphrase about a gamble, where any choice is as good as another
setter's reading: a warehouse where shoppers pay up front and carry their chosen goods away themselves

explanation.surface: A showman's patter at a fair: pay up and pick whatever you fancy.
explanation.walkthrough: The catchphrase 'you pays your money and you takes your choice' is read literally: a wholesale store where you pay on the spot and take the goods away yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash-and-carry is a wholesale warehouse where customers pay immediately and transport purchases themselves, with no credit or delivery.

clue.text: Took the bag round for money

definitions.text: Took the bag round for money

blocks.clueFragment: Took the bag round for money
blocks.note: surface reading: someone passing a collecting bag around, or a thief making off with a moneybag
setter's reading: carried a golfer's clubs round the course for a fee

explanation.surface: Someone did the rounds with a collection bag to raise funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A caddie is paid to carry a golfer's bag of clubs around the course, so did that job.

clue.text: Like a sound that's so nice when cut off

indicators.note: cut off means the end is lopped from the word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; it loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Praise for a pleasant sound that suddenly stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic means relating to or having the nature of sound waves.

clue.text: One who notifies a name not on the roster when it's put up

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name
taken as written
a rota is a roster of duties

explanation.surface: Someone announcing that a person's name is missing from a posted duty list.
explanation.walkthrough: A, N, NOT, then ROTA upwards as ATOR; 'notifies' is taken whimsically as 'adds notes to'.
explanation.definitionFit: An annotator adds notes to a text, so one who 'notes' it, a playful reading of notifies.

clue.text: Festoon the platform

blocks.note: first meaning: to adorn or decorate
second meaning: a flat floor or level surface, as on a ship

explanation.surface: Hang garlands on the stage for a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to decorate, as in deck the halls, and a deck is a floor or raised surface.

clue.text: Advertises excursion from the landing place

blocks.note: to air something is to make it public
a trip is an outing

explanation.surface: A travel promotion for an outing departing from a pier or landing stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a basic runway where aircraft can come down, a place for landing.

clue.text: A survival from the past remains

definitions.note: relic is singular; the plural relics is closer to remains

blocks.note: first meaning: an object or custom surviving from an earlier age
second meaning: the bodily remains of a saint, venerated as holy

explanation.surface: Something old still exists today.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object that has survived from an earlier era, or part of a dead saint's body kept for veneration.

clue.text: Parking allowed under elevated motorway, it's understood

indicators.note: elevated in a down clue means raised, written from the bottom up
under in a down clue places the next part below the other

blocks.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, read as MI
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
licit means lawful, permitted

explanation.surface: Everyone knows you can park beneath a raised motorway flyover.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 links London and Leeds; it is written MI here and turned upward to give IM, with P and LICIT beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Implicit means implied though not stated directly, so tacitly understood.

clue.text: Catch parent out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered, put out of place

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Catching a mother or father out in a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to snare or trick someone, especially into a compromising act, so to catch.

clue.text: Suitable place for a running buffet?

definitions.text: Suitable place for a running buffet?

blocks.note: surface reading: a buffet meal where food is served continuously, or a blow struck while running
setter's reading: a buffet that is literally running along the rails, served on a moving train

explanation.surface: Where best to lay on an all-day spread of food?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' suggests a continuous serving, but the meal is on something that runs: a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage fitted out for serving meals to passengers while the train is moving.

clue.text: Reverse call on the line from sweetheart

indicators.note: an instruction to read what follows from back to front

blocks.note: to call someone something is to name them; as a noun, a name
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A sweetheart's phone call comes in, and you reverse the charges.
explanation.walkthrough: NAME with L on it reads backwards as LEMAN, an archaic word for a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Leman is an old-fashioned literary word for a lover or beloved, often found in ballads and older poetry.

clue.text: Encourage one to quote without a note

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the other words go round

blocks.note: one is I, and to quote a source is to cite it, so 'I cite'
n. is the abbreviation for a note, as in a footnote reference

explanation.surface: Urging somebody to repeat words without a written prompt.
explanation.walkthrough: I CITE goes round N, giving I(N)CITE; the note is a footnote, abbreviated n., not a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to urge or stir someone up to act, a stronger synonym for encourage.

clue.text: One who is punctilious about the Liberal label

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: a sticker is an adhesive label
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Someone fussy about how the Liberal Party is labelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as concerning in the surface, but it is a placement instruction: the label wraps round the party's initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on exact observance of rules and details, which is what punctilious behaviour means.

clue.text: Authorise to install running water

indicators.note: to install is to put something in place inside something else

blocks.note: the Dee is a river, water that runs
to install is to put in

explanation.surface: Giving permission for a mains water supply to be fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Install' does double duty, supplying the inner word and saying where it goes. 'Running water' looks like plumbing but is a river: the Dee flows through Chester and Aberdeen.
explanation.definitionFit: To depute is to appoint or empower someone to act on your behalf, which is to authorise them.

clue.text: Their young are notoriously long-eared

blocks.note: surface reading: animals such as hares whose babies have long ears
setter's reading: the proverb that little jugs have long ears, meaning children overhear things

explanation.surface: A natural-history note about an animal whose babies have very long ears.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'little pitchers have long ears' warns that children overhear adult talk; a pitcher's handle is its ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitchers are jugs, and in the old saying their small offspring, children, have big listening ears.

clue.text: Drink that may go to one's head

definitions.text: that may go to one's head

blocks.note: first meaning: an alcoholic drink taken just before bed

blocks.clueFragment: that may go to one's head
blocks.note: second meaning: a soft cap once worn on the head in bed

explanation.surface: A warning about a strong drink that might leave you light-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to one's head' sounds like getting tipsy, but it is meant literally: something worn on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is a bedtime alcoholic drink, and also a soft cap formerly worn while sleeping.

clue.text: Calls to amphibious troops in rough weather

blocks.note: to hail is to call out to
taken as written
RM, the Royal Marines, fight on land and sea

explanation.surface: Shouting orders to marines landing in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Marines are Britain's amphibious commando force, abbreviated RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A hailstorm is a storm in which ice pellets fall, certainly rough weather.

clue.text: What are those men in the rear rank doing, shuffling about?

definitions.text: What are those men in the rear rank doing, shuffling about?

blocks.clueFragment: those men in the rear rank
blocks.note: surface reading: soldiers at the back of a parade fidgeting in line
setter's reading: chessmen on the back row, king and rook, swapping sides in a single move

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant demands why the soldiers at the back are fidgeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' are chess pieces and the 'rear rank' is the back row of the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Castling is the chess move in which king and rook on the back row move simultaneously past each other.

clue.text: Facts not new to Lamartine perhaps

indicators.note: not means the following letter is left out of the name
perhaps hints the remaining letters could be rearranged into another word

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new; it is the letter removed
the French Romantic poet Alphonse de Lamartine, taken as written

explanation.surface: Information that would be old news to the French poet Lamartine.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove N from LAMARTINE, then rearrange LAMARTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Material means facts or information gathered for use, as a writer's material for a book.

clue.text: Speedily moved a light sculpture

blocks.note: first meaning: able to move or be moved quickly
second meaning: a hanging artwork of balanced parts that sway in the air

explanation.surface: Someone hurriedly shifted a delicate statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moved' looks like a past verb; read it as an adjective, moved easily and fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobile means readily moving, and a mobile is a suspended kinetic sculpture like those of Calder.

clue.text: Police  back Corporation's pronouncement

indicators.note: back means the letters are read the other way round

blocks.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police forces
corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: The police support an announcement from the town council.
explanation.walkthrough: CID reversed gives DIC, then TUM; corporation in the sense of a paunch is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictum is an authoritative statement or formal saying, so a pronouncement.

clue.text: In column form, essential reading for the outgoing

definitions.text: In column form, essential reading for the outgoing

blocks.note: surface reading: a newspaper column that everyone should read
setter's reading: the silver column in a thermometer or barometer, checked by people about to go outdoors

explanation.surface: A newspaper column described as required reading for sociable types.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outgoing' suggests extrovert people; it means those going out, who check the weather glass before leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is the liquid metal whose rising and falling column shows temperature or air pressure.

clue.text: Live male creature -- a whopper

blocks.note: to live is to be, to exist
he is the male pronoun
a moth is one creature among many

explanation.surface: A living male animal described as enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creature' is a broad word standing for one particular small one, the moth.
explanation.definitionFit: A behemoth is something enormous, after the huge beast in the Book of Job, so a whopper.

clue.text: One very close to Scrooge

blocks.note: surface reading: a friend or relative intimate with Dickens's character
setter's reading: close meaning tight-fisted, a hoarder like him

explanation.surface: Someone said to be a close companion of Scrooge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' means stingy, not near or intimate.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards money and hates to spend it, exactly Scrooge's character in A Christmas Carol.

clue.text: Shylock keeping safe in old city

blocks.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia
safe as in certain, sure

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's moneylender holding his strongbox in some ancient town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe' looks like a strongbox but is an adjective meaning certain. Ur, the Sumerian city, is the crossword's favourite old city.
explanation.definitionFit: Shylock, the moneylender in The Merchant of Venice, is the archetype of one who lends at extortionate interest.

clue.text: Drink right up, and invest in another jar

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are written from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to tope is to drink heavily
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Knock back your drink and buy another glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jar' is British slang for a pint of beer, but here it is a plant pot; 'invest' means clothe or place in.
explanation.definitionFit: To repot a plant is to move it into a new or larger pot, so to place it in another container.

clue.text: Piles erected for the length of the bridge

indicators.note: erected in a down clue means set upright, written bottom to top

blocks.note: the pile of a carpet or fabric is its nap

explanation.surface: Supports driven in to carry a bridge along its length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piles' looks like bridge foundations, which suits the surface, but it is the raised fibres of a cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is the distance between a bridge's supports, or its whole extent.

clue.text: Peers at the ground

blocks.note: first meaning: members of the House of ..., the nobility
second meaning: ..., the famous cricket ground in London

explanation.surface: Someone peers across the field at the sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peers' looks like a verb for looking closely; it is the nobility. Lord's is the London home of cricket, ignoring the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Lords are members of the peerage, and Lord's is the best-known cricket venue in England.

clue.text: I am put out about concert being unrehearsed

indicators.note: put out suggests disturbed, knocked out of order
about means around, wrapping one part round another

blocks.note: contracted to I'm
taken as written
a prom is a promenade concert

explanation.surface: A performer upset that the concert has had no rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like annoyed, but only 'out' is the signal: the words 'I am put' get jumbled, and the concert sits inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Impromptu means done without preparation or practice, just as an unrehearsed performance is.

clue.text: It's more trying to get involved in this kind of mathematics

indicators.note: to get involved is to become entangled, mixed together

blocks.note: taken as written: twelve letters

explanation.surface: A schoolchild's complaint that this branch of maths is harder to engage with.
explanation.definitionFit: Trigonometry is the branch of mathematics dealing with angles and sides of triangles.
